Subject: SOC 2 evidence: snapshot cutover + log capture timing

Hi Marcus —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Brooks has a couple of follow-ups for our SOC 2 Type II ingestion to finish the evidence pack:

1) Audit period end: your report lists period end as 2026-09-30. Our auditor is asking whether you treat the end date as inclusive (i.e., data up to 2026-09-30 23:59:59 local) or if you rely on a point-in-time snapshot taken at the start of 2026-10-01 (00:00 UTC). Can you confirm how Redwood defines the boundary for the period?

2) Logs and endpoint captures: the auditor would like a short description of how logs are collected around cutover windows (for example, do rolling logs include UTC midnight rollovers and do you have OS-level log archives that could be sampled for a single timestamp?). A short matrix or bullet list will do.

3) Bridge letter: there was a 3-day maintenance window where a small feature rollout changed logging keys (2026-10-03 to 2026-10-05). We expect a bridge letter describing the gap and compensating controls — do you have a draft we can give Brooks?

Attached: request_checklist.xlsx with the auditor's required artifacts. Can you share a draft bridge letter and the log capture matrix by tomorrow EOD so we can keep the review on track?

Appreciate it —
Sarah
Sarah Dunham
Director, Risk & Compliance
Acme Corporation

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Dunham <sarah.dunham@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Audit Team <audit-team@brooks-assurance.com>

Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence: snapshot cutover + log capture timing

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and we'll follow with the attachments you asked for: 

- Audit period boundary: Redwood's Type II report uses an inclusive date boundary. For the 2026-09-30 period end, coverage includes events with timestamps up to and including 2026-09-30 23:59:59 in the customer-configured timezone for the tenant (we default to UTC if none specified). The auditor's point-in-time snapshot at 00:00 on 2026-10-01 is functionally equivalent to the inclusive end when logs are continuous; we will document both perspectives in the bridge letter to avoid confusion.

- Logs capture: we collect application and inference gateway logs with a rolling file append process and ship them to our central logging pipeline every 5 minutes. We retain raw logs in immutable object storage and maintain daily compressed snapshots at 00:00 UTC. OS-level journald entries are archived daily and available as read-only exports for audit sampling. I'll include a concise matrix that maps log type → collection cadence → retention snapshot.

- Bridge letter draft: attaching an internal draft (redwood_draft_bridge_letter_v1.pdf) that explains the 2026-10-03→10-05 rollout, the short-lived logging key change, and the compensating checks (replay checks, cross-validated request IDs, and access logs). We propose the language include both the inclusive-period statement and the snapshot equivalence note so auditors can choose.

I'll attach the log matrix and the draft now; Soojin and Neha are copied for any technical or controls clarifications. If Brooks wants a signed/dated version we'll send it through DocuSign.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_draft_bridge_letter_v1.pdf, logs_capture_matrix.csv
